newsitem.title: USA: Weather hampers search efforts in New Orleans.
newsitem.headline: Weather hampers search efforts in New Orleans.

text.p: Rescuers' efforts to search for victims amid collapsed sections of New Orleans' Riverwalk were hampered on Monday by rain, authorities said.

One end of the popular, upscale shopping strip overlooking the Mississippi River was heavily damaged on Saturday when the MV Bright Field, a Liberian-flagged freighter carrying 64,000 short tons of corn, lost power and ploughed into the mall.

More than 116 people were treated at area hospitals on Saturday, many for injuries sustained while trying to flee the mall and adjacent Riverside Wing of the New Orleans Hilton Hotel, where 125 rooms were damaged. A multi-storied parking garage also was damaged.

While authorities continued trying to assess the damage, the first lawsuit against the MV Bright Field's owner, the Cosco Co. of Hong Kong, was filed late on Sunday in federal district court in New Orleans.

Walter Lejier, one of eight attorneys filing the suit, said the plaintiffs include several Riverwalk business owners, residents of One River Place condominiums who had to leave their homes because utility connections were severed, and the owner of a car that fell from a parking garage into the river.
Legal experts said maritime law makes the legal entanglements surrounding the disaster more complex than a similar land-based accident.

Although no fatalities have been confirmed, officials conceded the hardest hit area, where four levels collapsed, has not been searched for casualties. "There was some shifting in that area and it hasn't been stable enough for rescuers to go in," city spokeswoman Michele Moore said on Monday.

"We will not stop the effort until we have searched and cleared all the debris," Fire Chief Warren McDaniels said. Officials said a crane may be brought in river to reach over the freighter and lift sections of debris for searchers.

A Coast Guard spokesman said the weather was posing some problems for tugs anchoring the damaged grain ship in place at the accident site. Divers have not been able to ascertain to what extent the ship is supporting the mall or determine damage to the underlying Poydras Street Wharf.

Officials credited river pilot Ted Davisson with saving hundreds of lives by dropping anchor to slow the ship, sounding the marine emergency siren and using limited steering capability to manoeuvre the crippled freighter between two docked cruise ships with 1,700 passengers and a riverboat casino loaded with 800 gamblers.
